findings.where: Article specimen: the red-orange bullets of the three-item list and the red-orange underlined link 'Streamlining the PPP Process…' in the PDF row (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: A red-orange appears on the article page that is not in the palette. The page's own palette card says 'four colours and no accent' and makes house blue the link colour. So this link is red-orange while the other link on the page ('Play again') is blue, and the list bullets take an accent the house colours do not have.
findings.who_objects: The founder, who asked for the house blue and grey as the only ink and every tile built around them, and who would find the article page has drifted off-brand. A reader of Mark's articles would also object, because links show in two different colours and nothing says why. Angélique would be left unsure which colour a new link should take.

findings.where: First screen: the blue field behind the whole hero, desktop and phone, set against the 'Texture' card and the motion-sketch field below
findings.fault: The hero's blue field carries dense diagonal pinstripes all over it. The Texture card says 'No texture: one flat field, no grain and no gradient', and the motion sketch shows the same field flat. So two surfaces meant to be the same field are treated differently, and the specimen describes a ground the visitor never sees. The stripes also run behind the heading, the lead paragraph and the caption, which makes the ground busier than one quiet colour field.
findings.who_objects: The founder, who said a ground's busyness is one of the three things to get right and who judges the first screen against what the tile claims for it. Mark would object too: he finds busy sites 'much too busy', and a striped ground drifts toward the drafting-sheet look this direction was meant to leave behind.

findings.where: First screen: the oversized pale-blue 'PPP' letters behind the heading (desktop), cut off as 'PP' at the right edge on phone
findings.fault: A ghost watermark in a lighter tint of the blue sits behind the heading's first lines. It adds a third tone to a field meant to be one colour, and it muddies the ground behind the largest white type. On phone it is cropped into broken letterforms at the edge of the screen.
findings.who_objects: The founder, who asked for one soft ground and 'a ground, an ink and at most one accent'. A visitor would also object, because the half-seen letters read as clutter or a rendering fault behind Mark's line instead of as his voice.

findings.where: First screen: the five white-outlined capsules under the lead (PPP Law, Infrastructure, Development banks, Governments, Risk allocation)
findings.fault: Static topic labels have their own white capsule edge on the blue, which is the styling of a filter or a button. The parts map shows that none of them can be acted on, so the surface treatment promises an action the page does not have, right next to the one real action.
findings.who_objects: A development-bank visitor who clicks a capsule expecting a list of Mark's work on that topic and gets nothing, and the founder, who wants one message and one action on the first screen.

findings.where: Nav lockup on the first screen, and the mark in the Texture card: the aqueduct mark and 'MMM INFRA' reversed to white
findings.fault: The logo is shown in an all-white version that is not among the versions Mark holds. His logo has the wordmark in blue #0070C0 and the arches in grey #404040. A white version is a new version of the logo, and it needs the client's yes before it is used.
findings.who_objects: Mark, as owner of the logo, who has not approved a white version. The founder would also object, because the tile then presents a logo version that is not Mark's as though it were settled.
